narrative: OMX30 opens with tailwinds from European strength and correlation support, trading 4.7% above the 200-MA in confirmed bull regime. However, technicals flash caution: Stochastic is deeply overbought at K=97.4, while RSI remains neutral at 57.6—classic mean-reversion setup. The +1.19% spike in US 10Y yields benefits financials (wider NIMs) but pressures real estate refinancing costs and tech DCF assumptions. Gold's +2.82% rally directly supports Boliden, while copper's +0.57% gain adds to mining upside. USD/SEK weakness and EUR/SEK strength favor large-cap exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson) despite NASDAQ's modest +0.82%. Key risk: ADX at 14.0 is weak, warranting 30% confidence reduction per mandate; combined with overbought oscillators, any earnings disappointment or geopolitical shock could trigger sharp profit-taking.

Technical structure is mixed: price +4.7% above 200-MA (bullish regime) but Stochastic K=97.4 screams overbought—watch for early-session pullback to 50-MA support around 3155. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) should outperform on US 10Y +119bp, widening NIM outlook; avoid real estate (Castellum, Balder) on refinancing cost headwinds. Boliden is the clear sector leader—gold +2.82% and copper +0.57% directly feed revenue. Exporters (Volvo B, Atlas Copco) benefit from USD/SEK weakness; Ericsson watch closely given NASDAQ +0.82% but sentiment fragile. H&M B a fade on EUR/SEK strength (sourcing cost pressure). Key level: 3180 (50-MA) is resistance; break below 3123 opens 3085 (Bollinger lower band). ADX weakness means conviction is LOW—use tighter stops and trim positions into strength.
